moduleTitle: Performing Data-driven Testing using Excel Files
learningObjectives: Explain the process for importing data from an Excel file into a test within Testim, ensuring effective data management.
Demonstrate how to run a test using parameterized variables to validate different outputs across multiple data sets.

elements.description: Test data files can be uploaded in CSV, JSON, or Excel, each up to 2 MB. When uploaded via the Excel/CSV route specifically, each row of the file is converted into a single data set, with a maximum of 1200 rows.
A single file can define multiple ordered data sets, letting one test run repeatedly against a whole matrix of input combinations instead of a single hardcoded scenario.

elements.text: Each column in the file becomes a parameterized variable a step can reference (the same Parameters mechanism covered earlier in this path) — a row is really just one full set of parameter values, and running the test 'with' a row means running it with those parameters substituted in.

bulletPoints: CSV / JSON / Excel supported, up to 2 MB per file.
Excel/CSV upload: one row → one data set, up to 1200 rows.
Multiple ordered data sets let one test cover many input combinations.
Columns = parameterized variables; a row is one full set of parameter values for a run.
Previously added test data is NOT auto-removed when new data is uploaded — it stays until explicitly removed.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Config File vs. Params File for data-driven CLI runs

elements.description: A Config File can override the Visual Editor's test data at either the execution level or a specific test level (via overrideTestData) — and it's also how an external data source (like a linked CSV file, or a database) is supplied instead of an uploaded file.

A Params File (JSON) is execution-level only — it applies the same set of parameters across every test in the CLI run, rather than being scoped to one specific test the way a Config File's overrideTestData can be.

bulletPoints: Config File: overrides test data at execution level OR a specific test (overrideTestData); also links external sources (CSV, database).
Params File: JSON, execution-level only — applies across every test in the run, not scoped to one test.
Both require running via the CLI, not the Visual Editor.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Where the multiple data sets actually run

elements.description: Running the test from the Testim Visual Editor only executes the FIRST data set in the file, even if the Excel/CSV has several. Only when the test is run from the Testim CLI, the Scheduler, or a local suite run does it actually execute multiple times, in order, once per data set.

elements.text: This is a common trap: seeing a single successful editor run and assuming the whole data set matrix has been exercised, when only row one has actually been used.

bulletPoints: Editor run = first data set only.
CLI / Scheduler / local suite run = every data set, in order.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming an editor run exercises every row of the uploaded data
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Uploading a 10-row Excel file, clicking Play in the editor once, and concluding all 10 data combinations were tested.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: The editor only runs the first data set. Run the test via the Testim CLI, Scheduler, or a local suite run to actually execute it once per row, in order.

practiceQuiz.scenario: When an Excel/CSV file is uploaded as test data, how does its content map to data sets?

options.text: The whole file becomes a single data set.
Each row is converted into a single data set, up to a maximum of 1200 rows.
Each column becomes a separate test.
Only the first row is ever used, regardless of run method.

practiceQuiz.hint: Rows, not columns, map to data sets — and there's a row cap.
practiceQuiz.rationale: After upload, each row is converted to a single data set, with a limit of 1200 rows. Columns represent the parameters within a data set, not separate tests.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A tester uploads a 5-row Excel data file, clicks Play in the Testim Visual Editor, and sees the test pass. How many of the 5 data sets were actually executed?

options.text: All 5.
Only the first data set.
None — Excel files aren't usable from the editor.
A random data set is chosen each run.

practiceQuiz.hint: The editor run has a well-known limitation here.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Running from the Testim Visual Editor only runs the first data set, even when the file defines several. Executing every data set requires the CLI, Scheduler, or a local suite run.

practiceQuiz.scenario: According to Testim's official documentation, what happens to test data already added to a test's Setup step when you upload a new data set?

options.text: It's automatically removed and replaced.
It stays in the test until it's explicitly removed.
It's silently merged with the old data, doubling the rows.
The test becomes locked and uneditable.

practiceQuiz.hint: Nothing is cleaned up automatically here.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Testim's docs specify that previous test data will not be automatically removed from a test until it's explicitly removed — uploading new data doesn't silently replace or merge with what's already there.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What's the key difference between a Params File and a Config File when supplying data-driven test data via the CLI?

options.text: A Params File only works with the Visual Editor, never the CLI.
A Config File applies its overrides execution-wide only; a Params File is scoped to one specific test.

A Params File (JSON) applies parameters across every test in a CLI run (execution-level only), while a Config File can override test data at either the execution level or a specific test (e.g. via overrideTestData).
Both apply only to a single, specifically named test.

practiceQuiz.hint: One of them can target a single test; the other can't.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A Params File is execution-level only — it applies across every test in the run. A Config File is more flexible: it can override test data at the execution level or scope the override to one specific test via overrideTestData.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Besides uploading a CSV/JSON/Excel file directly, what's another way to supply data-driven test data in Testim, per the documentation?

options.text: A live Slack channel feed.
An external source, such as a CSV file or a database, linked via a Config File.
A Google Calendar event.
A Chrome bookmark folder.

practiceQuiz.hint: The Config File can link to data instead of embedding it.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A Config File can link an external data source — such as a CSV file or a database — instead of relying solely on data uploaded directly into the test.

quickRecap.value: CSV, JSON, Excel — up to 2 MB per file.
One row = one data set (Excel/CSV upload), max 1200 rows.
Executes only the first data set.
Executes every data set, in order.
Not auto-removed — stays until explicitly deleted.
Config File = execution- or test-level override (+ external source linking); Params File = JSON, execution-level only.
